title: Modern Scams and Misalignments: Developing Resilience Through Awareness
primary_question: Can awareness of structural alignment help people and AI systems recognize potentially deceptive situations without teaching generalized distrust?
hypothesis: People and AI systems may become more resilient to changing forms of deception when taught to inspect structural alignment rather than memorize lists of known scams.

principles.trust: Do not grant more trust than the available evidence supports.

constraints: Misalignment does not automatically prove fraud.

student_protocol.name: Pause Inspect Verify

steps.pause: Determine whether action or commitment is being encouraged before the situation is sufficiently understood.
steps.inspect: Examine identities, incentives, claims, evidence, relationships, and requested actions for alignment.
steps.verify: Establish important claims through sources independent of the party making them.

student_protocol.fallback: If verification remains insufficient, do not escalate trust.

observer_model.principle: The landscape may remain unchanged while changes in observational position reveal previously unavailable relationships.

ai_role.preferred: Increase human awareness and assist investigation.
ai_role.avoid: Act as an unquestioned binary oracle of SAFE or SCAM.

learning_objective: Develop the ability to observe relationships and recognize when available evidence is insufficient before assigning or escalating trust.
stewardship_principle: Good stewardship does not teach people whom to trust. It helps them develop the awareness required to make better trust decisions themselves.
